description: All on-screen text for the VISOR client (English). Placeholders in curly brackets are filled from the bundle at run time; no measured number is typed here twice. Units: metres, minutes, degrees. Follows the HUD rules: information at the top, lower view clear, meaning never by colour alone, show reasons on demand, advise do not command.

app.title: VISOR
app.tagline: Measured, then used: the Mars map that corrects itself with what the rover found.
app.site: Gale crater, Mount Sharp boxwork. Curiosity sols {sol_first} to {sol_last}.
app.not_endorsed: Independent NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 entry. Not endorsed by NASA, JPL, Caltech, the USGS or the University of Arizona.
app.advisory: Planning aid only. Not flight software. Numbers marked 'assumption' are not measured.
app.credit_short: DEM: USGS (Calef & Parker) · Photo: NASA/JPL/UArizona · Rover: NASA/JPL-Caltech · Not endorsed by NASA

ui.sol_tip: Curiosity mission day ({sol_first} to {sol_last} cover the boxwork traverse)
ui.start_tip: Start time, local solar time. ✓ = sun {lo} to {hi} deg for the whole walk; ★ = best.
ui.t_chem: Curiosity's measured chemistry, one dot per target, at the rover's position when it measured (a target can be a few metres away). Colour = CaO (calcium oxide) wt%: pale <3, yellow 3-6, orange 6-10, red-orange 10-20, dark red >=20. Calcium-sulfate nodules and veins are calcium-rich. Large dots = APXS (contact), small = ChemCam (laser). Sols 4534-4843 (PDS release).
ui.verdict_tip: Advice, not a clearance: a route was found within the slope rule you set. The map's slopes are not validated at walk scale (see Risk).
ui.earth_date_tip: The Earth date when Curiosity lived this sol. Weather and radiation shown are records from that sol, not a forecast.
ui.st_range_tip: Likely range = p10 to p90 of {runs} uncertainty runs (map error, rover correction, speed, slope penalty, slope limit varied).
ui.stats_partial_tip: No route for leg {legs}: these numbers add up the walkable legs only.
ui.walk_blocked_tip: No full route under your slope rule: fix the plan before walking it.
ui.tl_blocked: No route on leg {legs}: stations past it are not on the timeline
ui.t_back: Lines of equal walking time back to the exit, every 2 min, from the route planner's cost map (your slope rule and pace). Beyond 6 min is faintly tinted; lines stop at 8 min. Display only: the field is smoothed over about 7 m so the lines read as rings (the HUD and cards use the exact times).
ui.s_trek: NASA Mars Trek · {x} m/px · view only
ui.t_trek: {label}, from NASA Mars Trek, {x} m per pixel over this patch. View only: slopes, routes and checks use the USGS 1 m DEM and 25 cm photo.
ui.t_photo: USGS 25 cm HiRISE colour photo: the measurement map (routes, checks and slopes use it with the USGS 1 m DEM).
ui.trek_failed: Could not load {file}; back to the USGS photo.
ui.trek_open: Open this place in NASA Mars Trek
ui.trek_open_tip: Opens trek.nasa.gov in a new tab. On a first visit Trek may open on the whole planet: open the link again.
ui.t_slope: Corrected slope: single hatch {caution_deg}–{slope_limit_deg} deg, cross hatch over the limit
ui.t_checks: ✓ within 2 deg of Curiosity's measured tilt, ~ within 3, ✗ more
ui.t_verified: Within {verified_radius_m} m of where Curiosity stood
ui.t_agree: Where the {runs} uncertainty runs walked; stronger = more runs
ui.t_ready: Vertical lines where this map's 3 m slope differs from an independent HiRISE DTM: sparse = {a} to {b} deg, dense = more than {b} deg. Result: {outcome}.
ui.t_shadow: Map-scale shadows; ridges 1–2 m tall cast none here
ui.data_list: MRO HiRISE photo and DEM · MSL PLACES positions and tilt · MSL Navcam photos · MSL ChemCam, APXS, CheMin results (stop cards)
ui.same_tip: Share of {runs} uncertainty runs that keep at least 90% of the leg within 3 m
ui.time_other: Range shown for the published plan only.

hud.minimap: Whole patch, north up: you (arrow) and the next stop (ring)
hud.view_third: Third person · C: first person · you are EV1 (red stripes); EV2 follows 5 m behind on the route
hud.goto: Walking to target: {x} m · steepest on the way {a}°
hud.tip_comms: Terrain line of sight from you to the exit (and to the suggested relay, if any), 1.7 m eyes, on the 1 m map: the 1-2 m ridges it cannot see may block more.
hud.ridge_strip: Ridge walls ~1–2 m tall (NASA) are not in this 3D ground: the 1 m map smooths them out
hud.ridge_tip: NASA/JPL, 23 Feb 2026: 'low ridges standing roughly 3 to 6 feet (1 to 2 meters) tall with sandy hollows in between'. VISOR's gate test found the 1 m map cannot resolve them, so the 3D ground here is smoothed. The 25 cm photo draped on the ground shows their pattern, but VISOR could not trace ridges reliably from it (ridge tracing check failed): look at the ground and the station photo, and expect steps the map does not show.
hud.tip_rover_tilt: Curiosity's own tilt where it parked, {distance_m} m from you (sol {sol}, PLACES): {rover_tilt_deg} deg over its 3 x 2.8 m footprint. The map's corrected slope here is {slope_corrected_deg} deg; on this spot the rover's measurement is the better number.
hud.tip_distance: Distance to {stop_name} along the planned route.
hud.tip_time: Walking time to {stop_name} at {speed_flat_mps} m/s on flat ground, slower on slopes (Tobler-shaped; assumption).
hud.tip_slope: Corrected slope under your feet: the map's slope at 3 m scale ({slope_map_deg} deg) minus {rc_bias} deg, because the map reads about {rc_bias} deg steeper than Curiosity measured.
hud.tip_back: Walking time back to the exit from where you stand, under the route's rules.
hud.rover_verified: Rover-verified ground: a six-wheeled rover stood here. Not verified for a suited human.
hud.hidden: Top bar hidden. Press H to show.
hud.no_way_back: No way back to the exit from here within the slope rule (assumption)

legend.title: Legend
legend.rover_check_agrees: Check mark: map within 2 deg of the rover's tilt
legend.rover_check_disagrees: Cross: map more than 3 deg off
legend.not_checked: No mark: not checked (anywhere off the rover's track)
legend.density: Pink shading: ground the uncertainty runs walked; faint = few runs, solid = most runs (key 8)
legend.shadow: Horizontal hatching: in shadow at the chosen hour, from the 1 m elevation map (ridges too small for it cast none here)
legend.verified_zone: White dots: rover-verified ground ({verified_radius_m} m around where Curiosity stood)
legend.slope_band_0: No hatching: corrected slope under {caution_deg} deg
legend.slope_band_1: Single hatching: corrected slope {caution_deg} to {slope_limit_deg} deg (caution)
legend.slope_band_2: Cross hatching: corrected slope over {slope_limit_deg} deg (route avoids it unless rover-verified; assumption)
legend.rover_check_tip: Sol {sol}: rover tilt {rover_tilt_deg} deg, map tilt {dem_tilt_deg} deg ({label})

layers.9: Shadows at the chosen hour (map scale)

limits_panel.title: What the map can and cannot tell you
limits_panel.gate: At 1 m detail the map cannot separate slopes from its own noise: {gate_patch_pct}% of this area reads 15 deg or steeper, but so does {gate_ref_pct}% of ground the rover found gentle.
limits_panel.rover_check: At rover scale the map reads too steep: median error {rc_median} deg over {rc_n} rover stops, map about {rc_bias} deg steeper. It still beats chance.
limits_panel.alignment: The photo and the map line up within about 2 m.
limits_panel.positions: Rover positions are accurate to about 0.5 m (PLACES).
limits_panel.not_modelled: Not modelled: spacesuit, Mars gravity, consumables, loose sand, rocks smaller than the photo shows.

assumptions_panel.title: What the numbers rest on
assumptions_panel.bias: Map slopes are lowered by {rc_bias} deg: the median gap between the map's tilt and Curiosity's measured tilt at {rc_n} stops.
assumptions_panel.speed: Default {speed_flat_mps} m/s on flat ground. NASA lunar EVA planning assumes {speed_src_lo} to {speed_src_hi} m/s for walking within a work site (Norcross et al. 2010, NASA/TP-2010-216115; Moon, not Mars). The slope penalty is Tobler's Earth hiking function, used the same uphill and downhill; suit and Mars gravity are not modelled.
assumptions_panel.penalty: Slower on slopes following Tobler's (1993) hiking function for people on Earth; used as a relative penalty, not a spacesuit model.
assumptions_panel.caution: The {caution_deg} deg caution band follows the Apollo slope classes (EPSC 2024 abstract).
assumptions_panel.limit: The route avoids corrected slopes over {slope_limit_deg} deg, except on rover-verified ground. See 'How sure is this route?'.
assumptions_panel.verified_radius: Ground within {verified_radius_m} m of a place Curiosity stood counts as rover-verified (set before the route was computed).
assumptions_panel.exit: The exit point is notional: no habitat or lander is there.

plans.add_tip: Click the map to add one stop to this plan.

plans.name: Plan {k}

cue.print_tip: One page per station for the crew (Apollo cuff-checklist style): map crop, times, question, tasks, bags, abort cue.
cue.title: VISOR cue card
cue.abort_none: If 30 min behind: no station to drop (the drill pair stays).
cue.foot: Suggested by VISOR from cited NASA facts; not a NASA plan. Map photo: NASA/JPL/UArizona (HiRISE); rover photo: NASA/JPL-Caltech (Navcam). Map slope is not validated at walk scale.

chem.title: Measured nearby (wt%)
chem.tip: Curiosity's ChemCam (laser, 2-7 m away) and APXS (contact) results for targets measured while the rover stood within {r} m of this station: wt% oxides, mean of each target's points; ChemCam iron is total iron as FeO (FeOT). Each target is placed at the rover's position when it was measured (the target itself can be 2-7 m from the rover); Dist. = station to that rover position. Sol = when it was measured, which can differ from the station's sol. PDS Geosciences Node, MSL release 42.
chem.col_dist_tip: Station to the rover's position when the target was measured (m)
chem.none: No ChemCam or APXS target within {r} m.

cond.title: Conditions for this EVA
cond.tip: Records Curiosity made on the selected sol (REMS weather) and on the stop sols (RAD): what the site was like then, not a forecast.
cond.none: No REMS weather record for sol {sol}.
cond.dose_v: ≈{x} µGy in {h} h, rover deck, not a suit dose
cond.dose_tip: Not from the selected sol: RAD silicon detector B, median dose rate on the {n} stop sols ({rate} µGy/h) × the EVA length. Measured on the rover deck, so no suit or body shielding; a dose in silicon, not an effective dose in sieverts.
cond.k_topo_where: Slope, route, walk-back, line of sight, 3D
cond.k_rover_where: Map vs rover check, rover-verified ground, Curiosity's path
cond.k_chem_src: ChemCam MOC + APXS oxides (MSL, PDS release 42); CheMin via NASA reports
cond.k_chem_where: Map layer (CaO), point readout, per-station oxide table, station facts
cond.k_chem_scale: 255 targets, at the rover position (a few m)
cond.k_thermal_where: Plan › Conditions; THEMIS in the Mars view
cond.k_thermal_scale: daily; THEMIS 100 m (too coarse for the walk)
cond.k_spec_src: TES (MGS); CRISM not on Trek tiles
cond.k_spec_scale: one TES pixel is larger than the patch
cond.k_sun_src: Mars24 model, checked against Mars Trek SPICE
cond.k_sun_where: Start hour, shadows, timeline, Walk lighting
cond.k_note: No orbital thermal or spectral map is sharp enough for a 0.6 km² walk; VISOR says so instead of stretching a blurred layer over it.

safety.ok: Plan check: fits the EVA, the route stays within your slope rule, and the partner-rescue check passes.
safety.ok_short: Ready: within your rules, fits the EVA, rescue check passes
safety.chip_ridges: Ridge walls not on the map
safety.ok_over: Plan check: fits the EVA, the route stays within your slope rule (steepest {worst}° corrected; {cells} route cells of 3 m over the {limit}° limit, all on ground Curiosity drove, which the rule allows), and the partner-rescue check passes.
safety.no_route: Not ready: no route within your slope rule. Change the stops or the rule.
safety.no_route_legs: Not ready: no route within your slope rule for leg {legs}. The numbers shown cover the walkable legs only. Change the stops or the rule.
safety.no_fit: Not ready: the walk and stations need more time than the EVA. Drop a station or shorten station time.
safety.no_rescue: Not ready: the partner-rescue check fails.
safety.under: Curiosity measured steeper ground than the map at {names} (up to {b}°)
safety.sight: the exit is out of sight for {pct}% of the route ({x} m)
safety.ridges: the map cannot see the 1–2 m ridge walls (NASA), so check the photo
safety.rule_tip: VISOR's ranking (a fixed rule, not a judgment): anything that blocks the plan first (no route, does not fit the EVA, rescue fails), then stations where Curiosity measured steeper ground than the map, then any part of the EVA after sunset or before sunrise (twilight, night), then losing sight of the exit (measured on the map), then the ridge walls the 1 m map cannot resolve. Where the map is steeper than the rover measured, the ground is gentler than the map: listed in Risk, not here.
safety.g_eva_v: Extravehicular activity: the time the crew spends outside in suits (here 6 h, NASA's planning value).
safety.g_sol_v: A Mars day (24 h 40 min). Curiosity counts its mission in sols; this walk uses what it measured on these sols.
safety.g_egress_v: Leaving and re-entering the habitat in suits (NASA: 1 h together).
safety.g_station_v: A stop where the crew does science: look, image, sample, compare.
safety.g_prio_v: Your priority for a station: must do, should do, could do. P3 is dropped first if you run late.
safety.g_pair_v: Curiosity's two drill sites, a ridge top and a hollow 10 m apart: compared together, never split.
safety.g_rover_v: At this spot Curiosity measured its own tilt. ✓ = the map's slope agrees with it; ≠ = it does not, in either direction: at some stops the map is steeper than the ground, at others less steep (both listed in Risk).
safety.g_corrected_v: The map's slope minus the bias measured against the rover ({rc_bias}° steeper on average at {rc_n} rover stops). It is an average: where Curiosity measured steeper ground than the map, the correction makes the slope look gentler than it is, so use the rover's tilt there.
safety.g_verified_v: Ground within 3 m of where Curiosity actually drove: known to be passable for a rover, not tested for a suited person.
safety.g_back_v: Time to walk back to the exit from a point, at the planned pace.
safety.g_runs_v: The route planned 1000 times with the map's errors and the walking pace varied: the spread shows how sure the times are.
safety.g_ltst_v: Local solar time at the site: 12:00 is when the Sun is highest.

ops.prio_tip: Your priority. Click to change: P1 must do, P2 should do, P3 could do. Sets what drops first if you run late.
ops.ground_tip: Map slope vs Curiosity's measured tilt here (rover check): {a}° vs {b}°
ops.pair_tip: Curiosity's two drill sites, about 10 m apart (NASA): kept together
ops.bag_tip: Bag labels are VISOR's short names for the sample tasks, not a NASA sample plan.
ops.no_route_tip: Not scheduled: no walkable route on leg {legs} under your slope rule, so the EVA timeline stops before this station. Move or remove the blocked stop, or change the rule.
ops.budget_aria: The EVA to scale: egress, walking, stations, ingress, spare time
ops.budget_spare: Spare: {x} min before the EVA length
ops.late_rule: Drops P3 first, then P2, later stations first; the drill pair stays together.
ops.late_short: Even dropping every station does not recover {x} min.
ops.late_apply_tip: Removes these stations; the route is re-planned exactly (walking time included).
ops.pick: Pick a station: click it on the map, the timeline or the Plan table.
ops.risk_ground_tip: Curiosity's measured tilt at these stops is far below the map's slope. The map is too steep here; the rover stood here.
ops.risk_under_tip: Curiosity measured steeper ground at these stops than the map shows (rover check: off by more than 3°). VISOR's map correction (map minus the average bias) makes these slopes look even gentler: plan with the rover's tilt here.
ops.ground_under_tip: Curiosity measured steeper ground than the map here: {b}° rover vs {a}° map. The map correction does not apply here; use the rover's tilt.
ops.unsettled_tip: These percentiles had not fully settled after {runs} runs (VISOR shows the wider of its two uncertainty runs).
ops.mars_clock: Times are Mars local solar time. A Mars minute is about 1.03 Earth minutes, so a {x}-min station (Earth minutes) spans about {y} Mars minutes.
ops.risk_sight: Out of sight of the exit
ops.risk_sight_tip: Line of sight between a person at the exit and the walker, both eyes 1.7 m (the app's eye-height assumption; no habitat or antenna height assumed). Terrain only: the 1 m map misses the 1-2 m ridges, so real sight is likely shorter. Out of sight = no direct visual contact and, for line-of-sight radio, no direct link.
ops.tl_sight: Out of sight of the exit (1.7 m eyes, terrain only)

plan_panel.robust_checking: Checking other slope limits in the background…

light.title: When to walk
light.intro: Start hours in local solar time. An hour passes if the sun stays {lo} to {hi} deg high for the whole walk (NASA Apollo guidance for the Moon; not tested on Mars).
light.ties: Among passing hours: least walking toward a low sun (under {low} deg, within {cone} deg of its direction; both assumptions), then least route in shadow, then the widest margin to the band. Time at stops not included.
light.none_note: No start hour passes on this sol; the nearest is {hour}.
light.sun_now: Sun at {hour}: {el} deg high, from {az} deg.

share.title: Share and export
share.hint: The page address always holds this plan: opening it gives the same settings and route.
share.copy_failed: Could not copy: the address bar holds the same link.
share.export_geo_tip: Route, stations (question, bags, walk-back) and rover-checked stops in longitude/latitude, for QGIS, JMARS or Mars Trek.
share.bad_version: This link uses an unknown format (v={v}); showing the published plan.
share.other_bundle: This link was made with a different data bundle, so numbers may differ.
share.bad_value: A link setting ({x}) was out of range and was ignored.
share.bad_stop: A stop in the link ({x}) is unknown and was skipped.
share.too_few: The link had fewer than two stops; showing the published stops.
share.export_what: VISOR EVA plan export: the plan, its settings and where every input came from.
share.export_how: To reproduce: open share_link with the bundle named by bundle.id. The plan is computed by crates/route-core from the bundle files listed here; their sha256 values match manifest.json.

brief.eva_verdict: {hours} h EVA: {n} stations of {x} min each, walking {walk} min ({p90} min at p90 of the uncertainty runs), {eg} h egress/ingress, {res} h emergency reserve held back.
brief.eva_verdict_typed: {hours} h EVA with your {x} min per station: {margin}
brief.eva_why: Station time = EVA length − egress/ingress − slow walking time, split evenly over the {n} stations (NASA EVA concept EVA-EXP-0042, pages 29–30; lunar, used for Mars). Each station has a suggested plan on its card.
brief.eva_changes: A longer walk, a shorter EVA length, or minutes you type per station in Plan › Crew.
brief.leg_chip_tip: Hover: find on the map · click: centre the map
brief.intro: What the existing results mean for this EVA. No new measurements; thresholds marked (choice) are design choices.
brief.drive_why: Spearman correlation of walking time with each input over {runs} uncertainty runs ({d} m terrain noise).
brief.drive_changes: The assumed range of {driver} narrows (for example, a measured suited pace), or another input's range widens.
brief.legs_why: Each keeps within 3 m of the plan in under {pct}% (choice) of {runs} uncertainty runs.
brief.legs_changes: The route changes. Agreement is known only for the published route.
brief.legs_other: Agreement is known only for the published route: reset the plan to see this finding.
brief.stab_changes: The slope limit moves outside the range above.
brief.map_steeper: On average the map reads steeper than the rover-driven ground: trust rover-verified ground first. Not at every stop: where Curiosity measured steeper ground, use its tilt.
brief.map_gentler: The map reads gentler than the rover-driven ground: map slopes may understate the ground.
brief.map_why: Signed median of DEM minus rover tilt: {rc_bias} deg at {n} stops. Held-out check: {outcome} (median error {a} deg uncorrected, {b} deg corrected).
brief.map_why_noheld: Signed median of DEM minus rover tilt: {rc_bias} deg at {n} stops. Held-out check: not in this bundle.
brief.map_changes: Rover stops outside the study sols show a bias of the other sign, or the held-out check fails on them.
brief.hour_why: Sun {el} deg (height / azimuth) at the start; {x} m walked toward a low sun, {z} m in shadow.
brief.hour_changes: Another sol, or a different sun band than {lo} to {hi} deg.
brief.rad_flat: RAD does not separate the stop sols.
brief.rad_why: Silicon detector medians {lo} to {hi} µGy/h over {n} stop sols; the smallest within-sol p10 to p90 spread is {x} µGy/h.
brief.rad_changes: Context only, never a route limit. A solar particle event during the walk would change it.
brief.wx_verdict: Sol {sol}: air maximum {hi} °C, warmer than {pct}% of study sols.
brief.wx_why: Rank of the air maximum among {n} study sols with a record (REMS outreach feed, values as given).
brief.wx_changes: These are outreach values, not the science archive (CAB disclaimer).
brief.strip_label: Air minimum to maximum on every study sol; the chosen sol is marked. Click to choose a sol.
brief.tl_weak: Least certain leg (under {pct}% of runs keep it)

readiness.summary_label: Readiness of every data source: count per status
readiness.intro: Is the map good enough here, and for what? Each row comes from a result already run (rule in the doc).
readiness.dem_verdict: Not for pixel slopes: gate {outcome} ({a}% of the patch at 15 deg or more vs {b}% on rover-gentle ground).
readiness.slope_verdict: Route planning after correction: the map reads {rc_bias} deg steeper than Curiosity's tilt ({n} stops); held-out check {outcome}.
readiness.prov_data: Map vs a second HiRISE DTM
readiness.prov_res: 1 m; the two sit {x} m apart
readiness.prov_verdict: {outcome}: 3 m slopes agree within {a} deg on {pct}% of the patch (median difference {z} deg). Key 0 shows where.
readiness.ridge_verdict: {outcome}: {n} of {total} NASA-labelled rover stops traced right, so no ridge layer is drawn. Ridges are 1–2 m tall (NASA); look for them in the photo.
readiness.sun_data: Sun position (our model vs NASA Mars Trek)
readiness.sun_verdict: {outcome}: within {a}° elevation and {b}° azimuth of Trek's SPICE sun (limits 0.5° and 1.0°, set before the run).
readiness.trek_verdict: Context only: the whole patch is {a} × {b} pixels in this layer.
readiness.trek_verdict_basemap: View-only basemap (Layers › Imagery): the patch is {a} × {b} pixels; lines up with our photo within {d} m.
readiness.trek_verdict_thermal: View-only basemap (Layers › Imagery): the patch is only {a} × {b} pixels, so it gives the setting, not the boxwork.
readiness.trek_verdict_coarse: Too coarse for the walk: the whole patch is {a} × {b} pixels, so it is not offered on the terrain. Useful at crater scale (Mars view).
readiness.trek_verdict_subpixel: Context only: the whole patch is smaller than one pixel of this layer.
readiness.trek_verdict_empty: Nothing drawn over the patch at {x} m per pixel (no mapped boundary crosses it).
readiness.trek_excluded: Mars Trek CTX Gale Crater mosaic
readiness.trek_excluded_verdict: Not used: it does not line up with the HiRISE products over this patch (checked by tools/trek.py).
readiness.photo_verdict: Ridges and hollows visible; matched to the map by a brightness fit, no correction applied.
readiness.places_res: about 0.5 m vs the base map (PLACES SIS)
readiness.places_verdict: Rover-checked ground: where Curiosity stood and the tilt it measured.
readiness.chem_verdict: Stop cards only; not a map.
readiness.rems_verdict: Context: {n} of {total} study sols have a record (outreach feed).
readiness.rad_verdict: Context only, never a route limit ({n} valid stop sols).

crew.title: Crew and margin
crew.hours_tip: Assumption: NASA ConOps gives 6±2 h EVAs (lunar).
crew.planned_tip: Optional. NASA gives no station time; type yours to see the margin.
crew.task: {hours} h EVA minus {x} h egress and ingress = {task} min for walking and stations (NASA ConOps p{page}).
crew.basis_plan: this plan's time; no uncertainty range for this plan
crew.avail: Station time available: {avail} min, about {per} min at each of {n} stops.
crew.margin_spare: With {planned} min at each of {n} stops: {margin} min to spare.
crew.margin_over: With {planned} min at each of {n} stops: over by {margin} min.
crew.reserve: Reserve, never planned in: {reserve} h emergency extension (NASA ConOps p{page}).
crew.go: Fits the EVA: walk and stations fit the time.
crew.no_go: Does not fit: walk and stations need more time than the EVA.
crew.rescue_pass: Rescue: from {stop}, walking back takes {wb} min; NASA requires an incapacitated partner at a safe haven within {limit} min (ConOps p{page}). A drag at {pct}% of walking pace ({pace} m/s on flat ground) still makes it.
crew.rescue_fail: Rescue: from {stop}, walking back alone takes {wb} min, over NASA's {limit} min to bring an incapacitated partner to a safe haven (ConOps p{page}).
crew.source: Values from NASA's lunar EVA ConOps; Mars EVAs are expected to be at least as long (p{page}), Mars walk-back ranges are still forward work.

mapkey.title: Map key
mapkey.back: Walk-back to exit: line every 2 min
mapkey.badges: Rover check: agrees · map off · steeper
mapkey.checks: Map vs rover tilt: agrees / roughly / off

science.title: Chemistry near each station (wt%)
science.tip: Mean of the ChemCam and APXS targets measured while Curiosity stood within 6 m of each station (PDS release 42). Dot area and shade = wt% relative to the highest station; the number is the mean.
science.col_tip: {name}: mean of {n} nearby targets. Click to open the station.
science.note: Targets are placed at the rover's position when measured (the spot itself can be a few metres away); ChemCam spots are a few mm across, so a mean is a guide to the ground, not a bedrock sample. FeOT = total iron as FeO.
science.pair_tip: Curiosity drilled both sites about 10 m apart (NASA): the ridge top and the hollow, nearby target means side by side.
science.none: No ChemCam or APXS targets near these stations.

drill.rover_note: Curiosity's own tilt, measured where it parked, against the map's slope over its footprint.
drill.chem_note: Placed at the rover's position when measured; the target itself can be a few metres away. wt% oxides.
drill.r_hidden: Out of sight of the exit
drill.a_fix_tip: The exit cannot be reached from this stop under your slope rule. This moves it to the nearest spot it can be reached from (it becomes a custom stop: Curiosity's facts stay with the original spot). Raising the slope limit instead is not offered: suited walking is planned below about 20 degrees.
drill.a_work_tip: Curiosity measured steeper ground at these stations than the map shows. The station stays (it is the science target); this places a W pin on the gentlest map ground 2-6 m away, about within reach, to stand and work from. Click a W pin to see its numbers, move it with a map click, or remove it. The map already read too low at the target, so check the ground there too.
drill.work_v: {x} m {label} · map {a}° (map read {b}° low at the target)
drill.a_relay_tip: Places an R pin on a spot within 6 min of the exit, on high ground, that sees the exit and as much of the hidden route as possible: a relay crew member or radio there keeps contact (Desert RATS practice). Click the R pin to see its numbers, move it with a map click, or remove it.
drill.relay_none: No spot within 6 min of the exit sees more of the route
drill.relay_note: Estimated on the 1 m map with 1.7 m eyes: the 1-2 m ridges it cannot see may block more. Dashed: still out of sight.
drill.profile: Height profile of this leg; hatched where the corrected slope is over your caution / limit

sim.sp_toggle: Show or hide this station's plan
sim.alert_unseen: Exit out of sight: check in, or use the relay
sim.alert_steep: Steep stretch ahead: up to {x}° over {d} m
sim.pano_tip: Curiosity's own Navcam 360-degree mosaic taken from this spot (PDS), turned to the way you face.
sim.pano_title: Curiosity's view from this spot · Navcam 360°, sol {sol}
sim.pano_note: Real photo, not a rendering: Navcam is black and white, taken from the mast about 2 m up, so the rover's own deck fills the bottom and black areas were not imaged. Drag or use the arrows to turn.
sim.navcam3d: Real 3D ground at your feet: Curiosity's Navcam stereo of the drill workspace (sol 4718), lighter = higher.
sim.navcam3d_tip: PDS Navcam XYZ product NLB_816331121XYZ_F1200082NCAM00309M1 (doi:10.17189/2pw6-a555), about 2.3 x 3.2 m in front of where the rover parked. Placed on the map by VISOR's Navcam check (its heights match the map within the check's limit) and raised by the measured median map-minus-Navcam offset. Centimetre-scale relief the 1 m map smooths out; everywhere else the 3D ground is the 1 m map.
sim.dwell_split: {x} min at each station: the time NASA's EVA numbers leave, split evenly (type your own in Plan › Crew)
sim.egress: Egress from the habitat ({x}; half of NASA's 1 h egress/ingress: assumption)
sim.ingress: Ingress ({x}; the other half of NASA's 1 h)
sim.plan_note: Suggested by VISOR from the cited facts (not a NASA plan). Inference marked.
sim.egress_note: Egress: suit checks and leaving the habitat. No science stop here.
sim.lane_eva_tip: The whole EVA on a time axis: egress, walking legs, stations, ingress, then the emergency reserve (hatched, never planned in). The line is the sun's height.
sim.no_dwell: Walking only: type minutes per stop in Plan › Crew to add station time
sim.csv: Download the simulated EVA (CSV, one row per second)
sim.manual: Manual: W A S D steer, Play resumes the plan
sim.scrub: Click or drag on the timeline to jump to that point of the walk
sim.daylight_tip: Sun {el}° now. Sunrise {rise}, sunset {set} on this sol, in local solar time (12:00 = sun highest; Mars24 sun). Curiosity's mission clock (mean solar time, used by the REMS weather feed) reads {y}. Twilight = up to 2 h before sunrise or after sunset (NASA Science). Light levels and sky colours are illustrative, not a sky model.
sim.dark_tip: Part of this EVA or its reserve falls after sunset or before sunrise. The twilight glow lasts up to 2 h (NASA Science). Start earlier to stay in daylight.
sim.lane_twilight: Twilight: sun below the horizon, glow up to 2 h (NASA Science)
sim.lane_night: Night: sun more than 2 h from the horizon

place.no_way_back: no way back under your slope rule
place.no_exit_sight: This spot cannot see the exit, so it cannot pass messages: it adds no contact. Move it.
place.far: Over {x} min from the exit: a relay this far cannot come back quickly.
place.out_of_reach: Over {x} m from the target: about out of arm's and tool reach.
place.work_note: Stand here to work at the steep target (the station itself does not move). Numbers are from the 1 m map: check the ground there too.
place.move_tip: The next click on the map puts the relay there; it is re-scored at once. Esc cancels.
place.move_work_tip: The next click on the map puts the working spot there (kept within 8 m of the station). Esc cancels.
place.remove_tip: Take this point off the plan.
place.cancel_tip: Keep the point where it is (Esc).
place.armed_relay: Click the map where the relay should stand · Esc cancels
place.armed_work: Click the map where the crew should stand to work at {name} · Esc cancels
place.use_work: Work from the safer spot ({x} m)
place.use_work_tip: Places a W pin on the gentlest map ground 2-6 m from this steep target, to stand and work from. The station itself stays.
place.set_work: Set a working spot (click the map)
place.set_work_tip: The next click on the map puts this station's working spot there (kept within 8 m of the station). Esc cancels.
place.show_work_tip: The W pin placed for this station: its numbers, Move and Remove.
place.work_placed_tip: W pins on the map: click one (or this) for its numbers, Move or Remove.
place.relay_placed: Relay placed: {a}% → {b}% of the route in contact
place.relay_blind: Relay cannot see the exit: move it
place.relay_placed_tip: The R pin on the map: click it (or this) for its numbers, Move or Remove. Terrain-only sight test on the 1 m map, 1.7 m eyes: the 1-2 m ridges it cannot see may block more.
place.pin_tip: Relay / EV2 position: click for numbers, Move or Remove
place.pin_work_tip: Working spot for {name}: click for numbers, Move or Remove
